Whether any single element holds the composition together is a question each work leaves open.","chapters":[{"title":"One Element in Charge","introduction":"These faces organize around a single dominant feature—an oversized head, a color boundary, a sealed gaze—that holds the composition together while smaller marks scatter around it."},{"title":"The Mouth Takes Over","introduction":"Here the mouth—teeth, jaw, open gap—moves from supporting feature to the part the eye reaches first, pulling attention downward and forward past everything else."},{"title":"Eyes as the Dominant Mark","introduction":"These works shift emphasis upward: eyes become targets, spirals, mismatched lenses, or single large orbs, each competing with the marks that surround them."},{"title":"Every Area at Equal Volume","introduction":"These works pack the face and the space around it so densely with competing marks, symbols, and color zones that the face becomes one element among many rather than the organizing center."},{"title":"Quieter Surfaces","introduction":"The final group: faces where the marks have settled into a particular register of color and line—not resolved, but no longer pulling against each other with equal force."}]}]}
